concepts.label: Paused state
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - third Function lifecycle state alongside deployed/undeployed (from deploy-eventing-functions.json); reachable only from deployed, and the only deployed-adjacent state where JavaScript is editable

concepts.label: Function log
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - user-defined diagnostic output stream produced by log(...) statements inside a Function's handler code

concepts.label: Checkpoint
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a saved point in the Function's mutation-processing stream, created on pause/deploy and used to resume without missing mutations

relations.subject: eventing:function
relations.evidence: You can only pause an Eventing Function when that Function has already been deployed.

relations.subject: eventing:paused-state
relations.evidence: You can edit the JavaScript code of a paused Function.

relations.subject: eventing:function
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - verb phrase for a lifecycle action producing a durable artifact; no existing predicate captures action-produces-artifact
relations.evidence: You can pause an Eventing Function to checkpoint the Function and stop processing document mutations. This checkpoint saves a specific point in the processing stream and helps you not miss any mutations when you resume the Function.

relations.subject: eventing:function
relations.evidence: You cannot edit the JavaScript code of a resumed Function.

relations.subject: eventing:function

relations.evidence: You can use Function logs to identify and capture activities and errors related to your business logic through user-defined messages specific to each Eventing Function.

relations.subject: eventing:function-log
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - no existing predicate models content-depends-on-code-construct; kept distinct from requiresSetting, which is reserved for configuration fields
relations.evidence: The content of the Function logs depends on the logic of the `log(…​)` statements you added inside the Function handler's JavaScript code.

relations.subject: eventing:deployed-state
relations.evidence: If your Eventing Function is in a deployed state, you can only edit some of its settings. To edit a larger number of your Function's settings, undeploy or pause your Function.

relations.subject: eventing:function
relations.evidence: Enable App Services Compatibility | Can only be edited when the Function does not share the same collection as an App Service.

relations.subject: eventing:undeployed-state
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - repurposing requiresSetting to express a state precondition since no dedicated 'requires state' predicate exists in the registry
relations.evidence: You can only delete an Eventing Function if the Function is undeployed.

notable_absence.finding: Every management action on this page (pause, resume, export, view logs, edit JavaScript, edit settings, delete) is gated exclusively by Function lifecycle state, never by a named privilege, capella-role, or credential type. Across all three core lifecycle pages in this batch (add/deploy/manage), Capella's Eventing UI documentation never names an access-control gate for function management - reinforcing the deploy-eventing-functions.json finding rather than introducing a new one.

cross_component_finding: The 'Enable App Services Compatibility' setting is now shown to be conditionally locked based on collection sharing with an App Service ('Can only be edited when the Function does not share the same collection as an App Service') - the collection is the unit of interop-conflict detection between Eventing and App Services/Sync Gateway, not the bucket or scope.
